about.title: Camarillo Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Camarillo's mix of freeway commuters and local traffic on Las Posas Road, Ponderosa Drive, and Santa Rosa Road adds up to hundreds of injury collisions every year, with 303 reported in the most recent full year and 411 people hurt. Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. see a noticeable jump in reported crashes, likely tied to weekend traffic building on US-101 and connecting surface streets. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: insurance adjusters often move fast, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. We're a personal injury team that evaluates your situation, explains your options under California law, and handles communication with insurers on your behalf, all on a contingency basis, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

about.ctaText: Get your free case review today — no obligation.

items.title: Time Limits Are Real
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but claims against a government entity — say, for a poorly maintained Ventura County roadway — can require notice in as little as six months. Getting in touch with us early helps make sure that clock doesn't run out.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a Las Posas Road or Santa Rosa Road collision, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. We can help make sure the insurance company doesn't inflate your percentage of blame.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: Unlike some states, California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. That means your claim can reflect the full impact of your injuries, not just medical bills and lost wages.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use these statements to find inconsistencies or minimize your claim later. Our team can advise you on how to communicate with insurers safely.

items.question: What if my accident happened on US-101 near Camarillo but I'm not sure whose fault it was?
items.answer: Fault isn't always obvious right away, especially in multi-vehicle freeway collisions. California's pure comparative fault rule means you can often still recover compensation even if you share some blame. We can help investigate the crash and gather evidence before it disappears.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Camarillo car accident?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, like the city or county, may be responsible for road conditions, the deadline to file a claim can be as short as six months. Because these timelines vary, it helps to talk with us sooner rather than later.

items.question: Does it cost anything to get a case review with us?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
